follow-up time: 3 months, with additional analysis at 1 year
outcome: Incidence of chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) three months after elective cesarean section (eCS)
cohort: 982 women who underwent elective cesarean section
finding: Women who consumed spicy food frequently (≥ 2 days/week) were more likely to experience chronic postsurgical pain three months after elective cesarean section compared to those who consumed spicy food less frequently (< 2 days/week).
mod_finding: Women who consumed spicy food frequently (≥ 2 days/week) were more likely to experience chronic postsurgical pain three months after elective cesarean section compared to those who consumed spicy food less frequently (< 2 days/week).
